- Backward integration into critical intermediates - indigenous processes developed for intermediates historically imported, stated to reduce import dependence, improve cost efficiencies and reinforce supply-chain resilience; a new intermediate plant on indigenous R&D technology was commissioned in FY2026
- In-house project engineering - the AR claims it 'enables us to commission new blocks and plants in shorter timelines and at lower cost than many of our peers, keeping our capital expenditure efficient as we grow' [provenance: Manufacturing chapter, capex_expansion bundle]
- R&D depth - two DSIR-recognised R&D centres focused on new molecules, intermediates, process improvement and yield; 28 new products (formulations and technicals) registered during FY2026
- Distribution reach - a dedicated sales force of over 350 professionals across 18 states, six zonal offices and 24 depots

- Regulated-market access - EU Technical Equivalence approval for a fungicide product, stated to improve European market access and support export growth

bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Chemicals management / process-safety hazard — BRSR material issue #1 (Risk, negative financial implication). The company manufactures pesticides, insecticides, fungicides and APIs, and identifies storage and handling of chemicals such as chlorine and CS2 and flammable materials like fuel as a major process hazard at the site. Mitigation: SOP adherence, scheduled inspections, Quantitative Risk Assessment, HIRA and HAZOP studies and engineering controls as advised by professional safety auditors and international clients' HSE auditors. This is the structural risk of the business model - a single incident is an existential, not incremental, exposure.
- Environmental compliance - waste, water and climate/GHG — BRSR material issues #2, #3 and #4 (all Risk, negative). Multiple processes generate chemical waste requiring regulated disposal (government-certified agents for landfilling, emission scrubbers, cyclones and dust collectors for boiler micro-waste, PPE management); water is essential to processes and contamination on use/disposal is a compliance exposure, managed through zero-liquid-discharge systems (RO, MEE, Spray Dryer) that are expanded during capacity increases. On climate, the AR states that companies failing to comply with GHG regulations 'may face penalties, reputational damage, and legal liabilities'; mitigation includes an initiated Product Carbon Footprint calculation, renewable energy for Scope 2, biomass for internal steam generation for Scope 1, and employee travel pooling for Scope 3.
- Occupational health and safety — BRSR material issue #6 (Risk, negative). Exposure of employees to harmful or toxic chemicals, plus a legal obligation to comply with OHS regulations. Mitigation: mandatory monthly health and safety training for all site employees, quarterly mock drills involving external safety inspectors across shifts, scheduled on-site health check-ups by empanelled doctors, and recurring HAZOP and HIRA assessments with external experts.
- Regulatory and legal compliance, including a pending income-tax block assessment — BRSR material issue #10 (Risk, negative): penalties, fines or legal action for non-compliance, which the AR notes may extend to 'prohibitions on corporate operations'; mitigated by an expert compliance monitoring system with action notification and internal inspection. Live instance: search operations were carried out by the Income Tax Department in December 2024 at, inter alia, the Company's business premises; a notice requiring a return of undisclosed income for the block period 01 April 2018 to 10 February 2025 was received and filed, a section 142(1) notice was responded to, and assessment proceedings are pending before the Assessing Officer. [provenance for the tax matter: BRSR Principle 1 Essential Indicator 2 (Non-Monetary), routed in the capex_expansion bundle, not in the risks_esg bundle]
- Single-activity and single-product concentration — BRSR Section A items 21 and 22: 'Manufacturing of Pesticides' is 97% of turnover and the single product line 'Pesticides' (NIC code 2021) is 97% of turnover. The entire earnings base sits in one regulated product category, exposed to the agricultural cycle, monsoon, crop mix, registration/ban decisions and agrochemical pricing - there is no diversifying segment. Not labelled as a risk by the Company.
- Export and single-state geographic concentration — Exports are stated at 39% of total turnover across 35 countries, exposing the Company to FX, trade-policy, freight and destination-registration risk; management separately flags supply chain disruptions, pricing pressures and geopolitical complexities. On the other side, every manufacturing site is in Uttar Pradesh (Dewa Road/Lucknow, Sandila/Hardoi, Hamirpur) and BRSR item 23 states 2 national plants with international plants Nil - a single-state operating base with no manufacturing redundancy outside it. Not labelled as a risk by the Company.
- Workforce structure and rising attrition — BRSR item 27: permanent-employee turnover rose to 22.49% in FY 2025-26 from 20.91% in FY 2024-25 and 18.76% in FY 2023-24 - three years of deterioration. BRSR item 25 shows zero permanent workers against 1,443 'other than permanent' workers, i.e. the entire worker base is non-permanent/contractual, alongside 1,126 permanent employees. Gender concentration is extreme (11 female employees of 1,126; 1 woman on a 9-member Board; zero women among 3 KMP). Not labelled as a risk by the Company.
- Dependence on imported intermediates and raw-material/supply-chain volatility — Management repeatedly frames backward integration as insulation from 'global supply volatility, particularly in relation to imports from China', and the Founder/Promoter Director cites fluctuating raw material prices, supply chain uncertainties and selective geopolitical pressures as FY2026 industry challenges. Until the ten-block Hamirpur build-out and further intermediate plants are commissioned, input security remains a live exposure. [provenance: 'Innovation-Led Backward Integration' R&D spread in the capex_expansion bundle and the Founder/Promoter Director's message in the profile and strategy_outlook bundles; the risks_esg bundle carries only the Corporate Overview version of the import-dependence statement]

outlook.body:
- Backward integration as the core strategic lever - developing indigenous processes for key intermediates, particularly those historically imported, to reduce supplier dependence, strengthen supply-chain resilience and improve cost competitiveness; management explicitly frames this as insulation from global supply volatility, 'particularly in relation to imports from China' [the China clause is back-filled from the 'Innovation-Led Backward Integration' R&D spread routed under CHAIRMAN / MD MESSAGE in the capex_expansion bundle; the strategy_outlook bundle carries the same intent without naming China]
- Capacity expansion as central to the growth strategy, with the Hamirpur facility positioned as the platform for specialty product manufacturing and future capacity expansion; supporting infrastructure and operational blocks stated to be progressing as planned
- R&D-led differentiation from DSIR-recognised R&D Centres focused on process improvement, cost optimisation and development of differentiated molecules, enabling faster commercialisation and higher operational efficiency
- Global expansion and deeper export footprint, with EU Technical Equivalence approval for a fungicide product as the stated entry step into the European market
- Formulations scale-up and domestic distribution depth - scaled formulations capacity of 10,000 metric tons supported by 24 depots and over 350 sales personnel across 18 states
- Alignment with 'Atmanirbhar Bharat' / 'Make in India' - building a self-reliant domestic manufacturing base for intermediates and reducing reliance on imports
- Process optimisation, operational discipline and customer alignment to sustain growth across key product categories
- ESG as an operating priority - renewable energy utilisation, waste management, green belt development and occupational health and safety standards, alongside the Samagra Sudhar and 'Chuppi Tod; Halla Bol' CSR programmes
- Reinvestment-led. The Company states that no amount was transferred to the General Reserve during the year under review and that the year's profit was retained in the business under 'Retained Earnings' (figures deliberately not reproduced). A Board-approved Dividend Distribution Policy is published on the Company's website under 'Policies', and dividend is stated to be paid after deduction of tax at source where applicable; no dividend rate, payout ratio, buyback, debt-reduction plan or credit rating is disclosed anywhere in the routed text. The Company states it has no funds contemplated under Section 125 of the Act lying unpaid or unclaimed for seven years, so nothing was required to be transferred to the Investor Education and Protection Fund; Mr. Narendra Ojha, Company Secretary and Compliance Officer, is the appointed Nodal Officer. On managerial pay, the 41st AGM notice proposes a special resolution for a 10% increase in the remuneration of Dr. Kuruba Adeppa, Whole-Time Director, effective 01st April 2026, performance-appraisal based, within Schedule V limits. [PROVENANCE: the reserves/dividend-policy/IEPF statements sit in the Board's Report text routed under the '=== MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION & ANALYSIS ===' heading in the profile, strategy_outlook, capex_expansion and risks_esg bundles - they are NOT in the governance_entities bundle. In this bundle the heading '=== DIVIDEND DISTRIBUTION POLICY ===' actually delivered Corporate Governance Report items 12.12-12.14 (insider trading code, PCS certificate of non-disqualification of directors, accounting-standards compliance) and contains nothing about dividend policy. The AGM remuneration item is from the Notice of AGM in this bundle.]
- Zero Liquid Discharge: liquid effluent from all plants is treated through RO, MEE and Spray Dryer, with treated water re-used according to purity and only final solid waste sent to government-certified agents for landfilling; ZLD systems are expanded whenever capacity increases. The Company states it has earned Zero Liquid Discharge certification [certification wording provenance: 'Building Capacity for the Next Phase of Growth' spread, capex_expansion bundle]
- Dated environment target: 'Aggressive initiatives to promote afforestation during 2026-27' (BRSR Section B item 5)
- Dated environment target: 'Increased use of solar power directly or indirectly during the Yr 2026-27' (BRSR Section B item 5)

- Renewable and low-carbon energy in use: 6 MW of captive solar power at the Sandila unit and biomass-based heat and steam generation; periodic energy assessments conducted through external experts [6 MW figure provenance: Manufacturing / Responsible Manufacturing spread, capex_expansion bundle]

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: IPL's expansion is built around three Uttar Pradesh sites - Dewa Road (Lucknow, commissioned 1991, 7 acres, fungicides, operating at near-full technical utilisation plus 6,500 MTPA formulations for the domestic market), Sandila (Hardoi, commissioned 2015, 23 acres, herbicides, the largest technical hub at 26,100 MTPA and the base of herbicide technical exports since 2018, with 6 MW of captive solar), and Hamirpur (25 acres, under development through wholly owned subsidiary Shalvis Specialities Limited, insecticides). Hamirpur is the stated growth engine: conceptualised as a ten-block integrated manufacturing complex, with common infrastructure - internal roads, civil works, boilers, utilities and chiller systems - established upfront so that new production blocks can be commissioned with significantly lower incremental capital investment and shorter execution timelines. Two production blocks are operational (Insecticides and Herbicides), two additional blocks are scheduled for commissioning during FY2027, formulations manufacturing commenced there in 2024 and technicals manufacturing commenced in 2026. During FY2026 the Company also commissioned an expansion of its Formulation Division, adding 3,500 MT per annum and taking formulation capacity from 6,500 MT per annum to 10,000 MT per annum, undertaken in view of strong demand (the sentence stating the demand rationale is truncated mid-sentence in the routed Board's Report text). Separately, a new intermediate plant based on indigenous in-house R&D technology was commissioned during the year, part of a backward-integration programme aimed at import substitution of key intermediates and reduced dependence on imports, particularly from China. Management states it is 'well positioned to increase our technical manufacturing capacity to 30,000 MT' from the stated 28,300 MT, and that in-house project engineering lets it commission new blocks and plants in shorter timelines and at lower cost than many peers, keeping capital expenditure efficient. No rupee capex quantum is stated anywhere in the narrative chapters; the only rupee capital figure supplied is a Capital Commitments named disclosure, which arrived without a unit line and is therefore not extracted (see capex_disclosed).
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Strong domestic demand, particularly for herbicides and intermediates
- Exports continued to deliver stable performance
- Improved utilisation across the Dewa Road, Sandila and Hamirpur facilities
- Formulations business demonstrated significant traction, supported by an expanded network of 24 depots and over 350 sales personnel across key agricultural markets in India
- Better realisations in domestic as well as export markets and improved demand across key product segments (Board's Report, 'State of Company's Affairs')
- Expanded formulations capacity and integrated manufacturing capabilities cited as reinforcing domestic and international presence
- EU Technical Equivalence approval expected to improve access to the European market, support export growth and boost export revenues
- Headwinds explicitly flagged by management: supply chain disruptions, pricing pressures, geopolitical complexities, fluctuating raw material prices and selective geopolitical pressures; the Indian agrochemical sector is described as having faced significant headwinds
- Management states it 'remains confident about sustaining growth momentum in the coming years supported by strong manufacturing capabilities, robust research & development infrastructure and expansion in domestic and international markets' - no quantified forward guidance is given anywhere in the routed text
- Strategic investments in plant expansions and a 'substantial capex allocation' are stated to be underway to enhance production capabilities, but no quantum or timeline is disclosed in the narrative

deepdive.thesis: IPL crossed INR 1,000 Cr revenue in FY26 driven by 30% volume growth and successful backward integration in herbicides, with FY27 guidance implying 15-20% growth as new Shalvis blocks and Hamirpur facility ramp up. Margin resilience (18-20%) is secured via in-house intermediate production despite global RM inflation, positioning the company as a key beneficiary of supply chain diversification away from China.

risks.note: BRSR material issue #1 (Risk, negative financial implication). The company manufactures pesticides, insecticides, fungicides and APIs, and identifies storage and handling of chemicals such as chlorine and CS2 and flammable materials like fuel as a major process hazard at the site. Mitigation: SOP adherence, scheduled inspections, Quantitative Risk Assessment, HIRA and HAZOP studies and engineering controls as advised by professional safety auditors and international clients' HSE auditors. This is the structural risk of the business model - a single incident is an existential, not incremental, exposure.

BRSR material issues #2, #3 and #4 (all Risk, negative). Multiple processes generate chemical waste requiring regulated disposal (government-certified agents for landfilling, emission scrubbers, cyclones and dust collectors for boiler micro-waste, PPE management); water is essential to processes and contamination on use/disposal is a compliance exposure, managed through zero-liquid-discharge systems (RO, MEE, Spray Dryer) that are expanded during capacity increases. On climate, the AR states that companies failing to comply with GHG regulations 'may face penalties, reputational damage, and legal liabilities'; mitigation includes an initiated Product Carbon Footprint calculation, renewable energy for Scope 2, biomass for internal steam generation for Scope 1, and employee travel pooling for Scope 3.
risks.risk: Environmental compliance - waste, water and climate/GHG

risks.note: BRSR material issue #6 (Risk, negative). Exposure of employees to harmful or toxic chemicals, plus a legal obligation to comply with OHS regulations. Mitigation: mandatory monthly health and safety training for all site employees, quarterly mock drills involving external safety inspectors across shifts, scheduled on-site health check-ups by empanelled doctors, and recurring HAZOP and HIRA assessments with external experts.

BRSR material issue #10 (Risk, negative): penalties, fines or legal action for non-compliance, which the AR notes may extend to 'prohibitions on corporate operations'; mitigated by an expert compliance monitoring system with action notification and internal inspection. Live instance: search operations were carried out by the Income Tax Department in December 2024 at, inter alia, the Company's business premises; a notice requiring a return of undisclosed income for the block period 01 April 2018 to 10 February 2025 was received and filed, a section 142(1) notice was responded to, and assessment proceedings are pending before the Assessing Officer. [provenance for the tax matter: BRSR Principle 1 Essential Indicator 2 (Non-Monetary), routed in the capex_expansion bundle, not in the risks_esg bundle]
risks.risk: Regulatory and legal compliance, including a pending income-tax block assessment

risks.note: BRSR Section A items 21 and 22: 'Manufacturing of Pesticides' is 97% of turnover and the single product line 'Pesticides' (NIC code 2021) is 97% of turnover. The entire earnings base sits in one regulated product category, exposed to the agricultural cycle, monsoon, crop mix, registration/ban decisions and agrochemical pricing - there is no diversifying segment. Not labelled as a risk by the Company.

Exports are stated at 39% of total turnover across 35 countries, exposing the Company to FX, trade-policy, freight and destination-registration risk; management separately flags supply chain disruptions, pricing pressures and geopolitical complexities. On the other side, every manufacturing site is in Uttar Pradesh (Dewa Road/Lucknow, Sandila/Hardoi, Hamirpur) and BRSR item 23 states 2 national plants with international plants Nil - a single-state operating base with no manufacturing redundancy outside it. Not labelled as a risk by the Company.

BRSR item 27: permanent-employee turnover rose to 22.49% in FY 2025-26 from 20.91% in FY 2024-25 and 18.76% in FY 2023-24 - three years of deterioration. BRSR item 25 shows zero permanent workers against 1,443 'other than permanent' workers, i.e. the entire worker base is non-permanent/contractual, alongside 1,126 permanent employees. Gender concentration is extreme (11 female employees of 1,126; 1 woman on a 9-member Board; zero women among 3 KMP). Not labelled as a risk by the Company.

Management repeatedly frames backward integration as insulation from 'global supply volatility, particularly in relation to imports from China', and the Founder/Promoter Director cites fluctuating raw material prices, supply chain uncertainties and selective geopolitical pressures as FY2026 industry challenges. Until the ten-block Hamirpur build-out and further intermediate plants are commissioned, input security remains a live exposure. [provenance: 'Innovation-Led Backward Integration' R&D spread in the capex_expansion bundle and the Founder/Promoter Director's message in the profile and strategy_outlook bundles; the risks_esg bundle carries only the Corporate Overview version of the import-dependence statement]
